newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent drifts lower after breaching support.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent drifts lower after breaching support.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures drifted lower on Friday as a follow-through to Thursday's sharp losses took the spot contract through a key support level.
August Brent was trading 14 cents lower at $18.07 a barrel at 1450 GMT having broken through support at $18.18. July gas oil was trading $1.50 a tonne down at $163.00.
"We broke through a key support and it looked like we're going to push below $18," said one broker. "If it closes below $18.18 today it's going to look very weak."
Brent shed over 70 cents on Thursday after local traders in New York led a burst of long liquidation.
U.S. markets were closed on Friday because of the Independence Day holiday.
"We saw a lot of buying earlier in the week as it looked like the market had more upside, but then it stalled and we saw some short-term long liquidation."
Next support for Brent was seen in the $17.90/$17.95 area and at $17.70.
News that Iraq and the U.N. had completed food distribution plans under the oil-for-food agreement helped push markets lower ahead of the long holiday weekend.

"Effectively the delay (in the resumption of Iraqi crude exports) is now in the hands of the Iraqi government, and everyone was concerned that further progress would be made over the long weekend," said brokers GNI in a daily report.
"Should the plan be approved by Baghdad then the whole process can go ahead quicker than the second week of August that most traders had been expecting," the report added.
One broker said that although the market has accounted for fresh Iraqi exports, a date for their resumption will still "take off another 20 cents".
The IPE Brent contract will close at 1630 GMT (1730 local time) on Friday due to the holiday in the United States.
